human_code: a page where the hasse diagram of the sentences is the only navigation: click a node to see its sentence and only the code it owns, everything else folded away

nodes.text:
the diagram of the sentences rules the page.
the diagram and the chosen sentence sit on the left.
they are the only navigation.
the code sits on the right.
nothing speaks until a node is clicked.

toggles and instructions do not exist.
the chrome is only the project bar top left and the file name above the code.

the compiler's json is all the page reads.
the page decides nothing.

a click on a diagram node selects it.
the node's sentence appears under the diagram.
the pane shows the sentence with its line breaks kept as written.
the code narrows to what the node owns.

a second click on the selected node clears the selection.
a click on the diagram background clears it too.

a hover on a node previews its lighting without selecting.

the code is cut at every range boundary.
each piece takes the colour of the deepest fragment that covers it.
specified is teal. assumed is ochre.

the code carries its real line numbers.
the file's name sits above it.

selection folds the rest of the code away.
every span the selected node does not own collapses into a thin fold.
the fold counts the hidden lines.

all the code the node owns is visible at once, without scrolling.

disk is the only source.
the page reads the project list, each project's map, and each project's code from it.

line endings are normalised.
what the compiler emitted is rendered exactly.

joint ownership is allowed.
a span of code may be owned by several sentences at once.
every span carries all of its owners.

lighting one owner lights its co-owners wherever ownership is joint.

the sentences are drawn as a layered graph of range containment, on the left.
covering edges only; transitive edges never.
the root sits on top.

a sentence hangs below every parent whose range most tightly contains one of its own.
several parents are allowed.
the folder tree cannot show that.

the ownership index lives in the page.
it answers which spans a sentence owns, and which sentences own a span.

every span listens.
hovering code lights every owning sentence in the diagram.

assumed fragments get nodes of their own in the diagram.
each hangs under whatever contains it.
each is drawn in ochre.

its text is the why it carries.
clicking it shows only the code it owns.

the project name sits top left, behind a left caret.
the caret opens the projects view.

that view is a plain list of every project and its human_code.
choosing a project opens its page.

a synthetic node is treated like a sentence.
the pane shows its why in ochre.
the diagram lists it, layers it, and draws it beside the real ones.

map.why: the html scaffold and the glue between blocks — doctype, head, tag seams, the script wrapper. plumbing the page implies but no sentence describes
the whole look — colours, spacing, light and dark theme. chosen by convention, nobody asked for it
html escaping glue so code renders as text, demanded by the medium not by a sentence
